📺 Lucifer (2016–2021)

Lucifer follows Lucifer Morningstar, the charming and rebellious Devil who grows tired of ruling Hell and decides to abandon his throne for a new life in Los Angeles. After opening a luxurious nightclub called Lux, Lucifer becomes involved in a murder investigation that introduces him to Detective Chloe Decker, a determined police officer who seems strangely immune to his supernatural abilities. Fascinated by Chloe, Lucifer begins working alongside the LAPD as a civilian consultant, using his extraordinary powers to uncover criminals’ deepest desires and solve mysterious cases. As their partnership develops, Lucifer must confront complicated family relationships, celestial conflicts, and unexpected feelings that challenge everything he believes about himself. Starring Tom Ellis and Lauren German, the series combines supernatural mysteries, hilarious comedy, romance, and emotional drama while exploring love, redemption, identity, and the possibility of change.

🎭 Genre: Fantasy • Crime • Drama • Mystery • Romance

⭐ IMDb: 8.0/10

⏱️ Runtime: Approximately 42–60 minutes per episode • TV-14

🎥 Developer: Tom Kapinos

📚 Based On: The DC Comics character created by Neil Gaiman, Sam Kieth, and Mike Dringenberg.

📺 Where to Watch: Netflix in the United States.

source_details.synopsis: Lucifer is an American urban fantasy television series developed by Tom Kapinos that began airing on January 25, 2016, and concluded on September 10, 2021. It revolves around Lucifer Morningstar (Tom Ellis), an alternate version of the DC Comics character of the same name created by Neil Gaiman, Sam Kieth and Mike Dringenberg. In the series, Lucifer, the devil, abandons Hell to run a nightclub in Los Angeles, subsequently experiencing massive life changes when he becomes a consultant to the Los Angeles Police Department.
